title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is a continuation of Grothendieck's study of the 'locally compatible' (lacet-preserving) outer automorphisms u of the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3} of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Equivalently, these are automorphisms of the profinite Teichmüller groupoid Ĝ^+_{0,3} that are compatible with the S_3 = G_3 symmetry. This group, Autext_lc(π̂_{0,3})' ≅ Autext_lc(Ĝ^+_{0,3})', is a version of what was later called the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group ĜT, and Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q) maps into it. Each u has several invariants:
- the multiplicator p = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ^×, the cyclotomic character when u comes from Γ_Q;
- γ ∈ Ẑ with p = 2γ+1 (next page: p=1 ⇔ γ=0, and p=−1 gives γ=−1). This is Drinfeld's m = (λ−1)/2;
- g ∈ π̂_{0,3}, the analogue of Drinfeld/Ihara's f_σ.

Previous page. The defining conditions on u were rewritten as two non-abelian 1-cocycle equations (73):
- ξ·ρ(ξ)·ρ²(ξ) = 1 for Z/3 acting through the order-3 rotation ρ;
- h_0·σ_∞(h_0) = 1 for Z/2 acting through σ_∞.
These are solved parametrically as coboundaries (74): ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} (or λh_0^{-1}ρ(λ)^{-1}, depending on p mod 3) and h_0 = g_0^{-1}σ_∞(g_0)^α. Here g_0 is a 'square-root' parameter for the 2-cycle relation, and g itself has a parametric representation (58) involving λ_0.

This page, item 3. The relation between the two coboundary parameters is read off from the second expression (62) of g: λ_0 = g_0 h_0^{-γ} λ (75).

Item 4. All these quantities are well defined only up to stated indeterminacies, with p ∈ Ẑ^×, γ ∈ Ẑ, g ∈ π̂_{0,3}, g_0 ∈ π̂_{0,3}/L_0 (L_0 = inertia at 0), etc. They can therefore be viewed as functions on the group Autext_lc(π̂_{0,3})', valued in Ẑ^×, Ẑ, π̂_{0,3}, π̂_{0,3}/L_0, …. Restricting along Γ_Q → Autext_lc gives particular functions on Γ_Q, valued in profinite spaces, which transform via the cyclotomic character.

Margin. Grothendieck writes that one would very much like these 'universal functions' g_0 (and hence h_0, ζ, λ, λ_0) to be arithmetically meaningful. This is the question of an arithmetic interpretation of the GT-coordinates of Galois elements beyond the cyclotomic character.

Purpose. The aim is to parametrize ĜT-type elements by coboundary data and to find explicit elements; the next page laments that only u = 1 and complex conjugation τ_∞ are known explicitly.
errors: Possible inconsistency with the next page's example u = τ_∞. There γ = −1 and h_0 = 1, so (75) gives λ_0 = g_0 λ. With the bracketed values λ_0 = τ_∞ and λ = l_0^{-1}τ_∞ this would need g_0 = l_0 (mod indeterminacy), whereas the next page states g_0 = 1. Since g_0 lives only in π̂_{0,3}/L_0, the discrepancy can be absorbed by the indeterminacy, but the bookkeeping is not fully consistent as written.

Item 4 says the quantities are 'functions' on Autext_lc, but several (g_0, λ, λ_0) are only defined up to the indeterminacies listed. They are really sections of torsors or multivalued functions, not canonical functions, unless normalized; Grothendieck seems aware of this ('avec les indéterminations').

ideas.what: Writing the two-cycle and three-cycle defining relations of (what became) ĜT as non-abelian 1-cocycle conditions for Z/2 and Z/3 acting on π̂_{0,3}, and solving them as coboundaries with parameters g_0, λ; the relation (75) links the parameters.
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological interpretation of the defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, 'A cohomological interpretation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group' (Invent. Math. 1997); also related work of Nakamura and Schneps
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse; possibly within the circulated Longue Marche material (unsure)

ideas.what: Viewing the coordinates (p, γ, g, g_0, h_0, ζ, λ, λ_0) as universal (multi-valued) functions on Autext_lc(π̂_{0,3})', and by restriction on Γ_Q, transforming via the cyclotomic character.
ideas.modern_name: Coordinates on ĜT and the Ihara/Drinfeld cocycle f_σ (Γ_Q → ĜT, σ ↦ (χ(σ), f_σ))
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and Γ_Q action qualitatively, without these coordinates

ideas.what: Wish that the universal functions g_0, h_0, ζ, λ, λ_0 restricted to Γ_Q have arithmetic meaning.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic interpretation of f_σ: Ihara's power series, Jacobi sums and Anderson's hyperadelic gamma function, Soulé characters

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for an arithmetic interpretation not only of g ≈ f_σ but of the auxiliary coboundary parameters g_0 (a 'square root' of the Z/2 cocycle) and λ, λ_0 (trivializations of the Z/3 cocycle) as functions on Γ_Q. Known arithmetic results (Ihara–Anderson–Coleman, Soulé characters) concern f_σ and its metabelian image, not these normalized coboundary parameters.
missed.quote: On aurait envie (à mon avis!) que les fonctions universelles g_0, et par là aussi ... h_0, ζ, λ, λ_0 ... soient ... signifiantes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Path-torsor interpretations give f_σ = p^{-1}σ(p), and g_0 looks like a 'half-path' (e.g. to a symmetric point such as the tangential base point at 1/2 or −1). Identifying g_0 and λ, e.g. via paths to the fixed points of σ_∞ and ρ, would give finer Galois invariants. This is plausible but not systematically treated in the literature.

missed.claim: Grothendieck had the cocycle/coboundary parametrization of the defining relations of ĜT (73)–(75), anticipating Lochak–Schneps 1997. This includes the relation between the Z/2 and Z/3 coboundary parameters and the fact that their indeterminacies are governed by inertia subgroups L_0.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Priority/credit. It also shows the cohomological viewpoint was Grothendieck's own route into the 'equation des lacets'.

deep.surprise_reason: The cocycle/coboundary reading of the GT relations matches later published work (Lochak–Schneps), so it is mostly a priority detail. The explicit wish for arithmetic meaning of the auxiliary parameters g_0, λ is a modest unexplored thread.
transcription_corrections: 'représentation principale' should read 'représentation paramétrique' (of g, eq. (58)).
The variable written ζ on this page is the same as ξ on the neighbouring pages (it is the Z/3 cocycle).
The membership list should align roughly as p ∈ Ẑ^×, γ ∈ Ẑ, g ∈ π̂_{0,3}, g_0 ∈ π̂_{0,3}/L_0, with λ ∈ π̂_{0,3}. The machine transcription shifts the targets.
The margin likely begins 'On aurait envie! (et à mon avis!)'.
The last line likely reads something like '... se transformant par le caractère cyclotomique' rather than 'commutant par la connection cyclotomique' (uncertain).
The phrase after 'les quantités' contains inserted λ_0', λ' with a hard-to-read addition, possibly 'jointes au moment'.
